text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
* Taxpayers are going to have to fork out around N$3 million to pay for the cost of transporting Namibia's 98-strong delegation to and from the World Festival for Youth and Students in Cuba.
* The deadline for submissions on the Affirmative Action Bill will remain August 18, despite concerns that the timeframe for submitting comments on the bill was too short.
* Political pressure is increasing to restructure the meat marketing company Meatco, whose board of directors currently comprises four elected and two government-appointed directors.
* The Castle Lager Brave Warrior's qualification for the African Nations Cup final has opened new doors for Namibian football.

* Speculation that U.S. president Bill Clinton may visit Namibia before the end of the year is increasing with diplomats saying Clinton will most definitely pay South African president Nelson Mandela a visit and will thereafter stop-over in a few key-countries on the continent.
